newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 5.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 5.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday:

** Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral calls for tighter regulatory controls over finance firms after CRB Capital Markets Ltd was charged with financial irregularities, an official spokesman says after the PM met with officials from the Central Bureau of Investigation and the Finance Ministry

"He urged the officials to take steps to protect the interests of common investors. He also asked the officials to take legal remedies and evolve a corrective mechanism to prevent recurrence of such trends," he says
** India's exports fall sharply in April, the government reports, but analysts attribute the decline largely to temporary factors including an 11-day truck strike
The Commerce Ministry says exports fell by 10.1 percent in April to $2.52 billion from $2.81 billion in April 1996
** State-controlled crude oil refiner Cochin Refineries Ltd hopes to resume operations, halted earlier this week because of a water shortage, on Friday, a company spokesman says
"We hope to resume operations by Friday evening," company spokesman Sajeev Nair told Reuters by telephone on Thursday from Cochin city in the southern state of Kerala
** The plan for a fully convertible rupee by the turn of the century poses the problem of stopping an overvalued currency getting stronger, analysts say
Rajan Govil, economist at securities firm HSBC B&K, reckons the Reserve Bank of India will have to engineer a weaker rupee soon, helped by a slowdown in capital inflows
** An official panel's recommendations to make the rupee convertible on the capital account within three years will whet the country's rising appetite for offshore debt, analysts say
"This will stimulate demand for offshore debt," Rana Kapoor, general manager, corporate finance and capital markets at ANZ Grindlays Bank, says
** Bajaj Electricals announces it will offer one bonus share for every two equity shares held
** The net profit of diversified firm Raymond Ltd plunges to 88.84 million rupees in the year ended March 31, from 957.61 million in the previous year
MARKETS:
** Bombay's benchmark stocks index .BSESN closes 22.57 points, or 0.59 percent, higher at 3861.42 on Wednesday
** The Delhi share index gains 4.56 points to 807.49, Madras jumps 95.66 points to 3,853.69 and Calcutta rises 1.21 points to 109.42
** Indian rupee opens unchanged at 35.76/77 against the dollar on Thursday. Dealers see the rupee testing the 35.75-mark against dollar unless the Reserve Bank of India intervenes
** The day's range seen at 35.75/78 in RBI's absence.
** The 10 percent year-on-year fall in Indian exports in April largely reflects the impact of the overvalued rupee on exports, some dealers say
